newsitem.title: FRANCE: FORECAST-Algeria budgets $1.54 bln 1997 deficit. [CORRECTED 12:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Algeria budgets $1.54 bln 1997 deficit. [CORRECTED 12:40 GMT]

text.p: Algeria's draft budget forecasts income at 829.4 billion dinars (corrects from dirhams) ($15.08 billion) in 1997 with spending at 914.1 billion dinars (corrects from dirhams) ($16.62 billion), the official Algerian news agency APS said on Wednesday.
The agency quoted Finance Minister Abdelkrim Harchaoui as saying the budget also forecast five percent economic growth in 1997. This compared with an envisaged growth of 4.4 percent in 1996.
APS said the OPEC-member's budget was based on an average price of $17.50 per barrel of oil.
The draft forecasts inflation for 1997 at an annual rate of 10 percent. Inflation for this year was estimated at some 19 percent.

Spending will be divided between operating expenses set at 640.6 billion dinars and equipment at 273.5 billion, the agency said. The draft budget, already approved by the cabinet, was being discussed on Wednesday by the National Transitional Council, an appointed body acting as a quasi-parliament in the absence of an elected assembly.
